subject: StratusCare VPC: intermittent decoder errors and throughput collapse - coordination
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratuscare.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: adam.berg@stratuscare.com
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Connor —

We started seeing a large p95/99 jump in our private VPC yesterday evening around 22:10 UTC. Errors are primarily decoder 5xx (502/504) and we also observed a sustained throughput drop (~40% lower tokens/s) across a subset of nodes. Attached is a short screenshot of the p95 trend and one kvcache snapshot that SRE captured.

This is impacting our triage pipeline (batch inference) and the UI timeouts for support flows. Can Redwood confirm whether anything changed on your side (model variant, kernel updates, routing)? We’re on the private package with pinned model v3.2.1 and custom quant profile.

We need an operational plan and ETA for mitigation — if you can loop in an ops lead and someone who owns the private runtime tuning, that’d help.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
SRE Lead, StratusCare
(Attachment: p95_trend_stratuscare_20261110.png, kvcache_snapshot_20261110.tar.gz)

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratuscare.com>, adam.berg@stratuscare.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Maria — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I’m sorry you’re seeing this. Quick notes:

- I’ve opened INF-9821 in our triage queue and flagged it P1.
- Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Evelyn (SRE for Private runtime) to lead the investigation.
- Can you confirm whether the affected workloads are heavy in long-context decoding (>=2048 tokens) or short requests? Also whether you observe increased concurrency from your side around the same window.

We’ll start with an initial blast radius & fallback assessment and share a short remediation plan within 2 hours. If a fast fallback to a hosted-compatible model variant is acceptable as a temporary mitigation we can enable it while we tune.

—Connor
Connor O’Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Picked this up — initial triage notes below:

1) Short summary of telemetry we pulled (preliminary):
   - P95 token latency spiked from ~320ms to ~1.4s starting at 22:08 UTC.
   - 502/504 error rate rose from ~0.1% -> ~3.6% for decoder ops.
   - Throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~35% on three racks of nodes (node IDs: vc-11-*, vc-12-*, vc-13-*).

2) Candidate root causes we are exploring:
   - KV cache pressure: we see cache eviction storms correlated with the spike window. A misaligned workload (large burst of long-context requests) likely forced heavy KV traffic and increased kernel stalls.
   - Quantization mismatch/regression on the recent customer quant profiles: while model binary is pinned, runtime kernel selection changed on a subset of nodes due to a nondisruptive scheduler change; some nodes picked an alternate int8 kernel path that is currently slower under long contexts.
   - Network pinning: not seeing obvious cross-region routing shifts, but we’ll validate NIC interrupts and driver queues for vc-12.

3) Immediate actions suggested (short window mitigations):
   - Reduce per-request max context to 1024 for the affected route (config toggle) — should reduce KV pressure.
   - Evict and rebuild KV caches on vc-11/12/13 during a rolling window (we can trigger low-impact restarts to clear starving cache shards).
   - Pin kernel selection back to the previously observed preferred kernel for these private nodes (hotpatch config).

I’ll prepare a hotpatch plan and an ops runbook for the rolling cache rebuild. Need Marissa to confirm whether we can temporarily throttle client concurrency and whether StratusCare will accept a short (~30 min avg) canary-fallback to hosted variant while we tune.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
SRE — Private Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratuscare.com>, connor.obrien@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Maria / Adam —

We can run the mitigations Evelyn outlined. Operational asks from our side:

- StratusCare to confirm a 60-minute maintenance window where client traffic can be throttled to 30% of baseline for the rolling kvcache refresh. This minimizes impact while we rebuild caches.
- Approval to toggle max context to 1024 for the affected inference route (we can revert after).
- If you accept a host fallback, we’ll route 10% of traffic to a hosted model variant (same weights) as a canary to validate end-to-end latency and error reduction.

Attached: hotpatch_plan_v1.md — contains step-by-step (rollback included). If you approve, we’ll schedule the window as soon as today 18:30 UTC or tomorrow morning depending on your ops team.

Also cc’ing Laura — she’ll be the escalation contact for exec communication and SLA note.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: hotpatch_plan_v1.md)

From: Adam Berg <adam.berg@stratuscare.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratuscare.com>, procurement@stratuscare.com
Date: 2026-11-10T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Thanks — we can take the 60-minute window tonight at 18:30 UTC. Maria will throttle client retries and we’ll cap concurrency at 30%. Approval for:

- Context cap to 1024: APPROVED (for the route in question).
- 10% hosted canary fallback: APPROVED for an immediate canary (please monitor for data exfil concerns — we’re under a strict data residency clause but fallbacks to the Redwood hosted testing cluster are permitted under our contract when masked).

Please confirm the exact rollback criteria and who will own the escalation if errors spike during the hotpatch.

—Adam
Adam Berg
Platform Lead, StratusCare

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratuscare.com>, adam.berg@stratuscare.com
Date: 2026-11-12T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + decoder 5xx in our VPC (urgent)

Post-mortem + exec note (summary for StratusCare exec sync):

- What happened: A KV cache eviction cascade combined with an unintended kernel selection variance on three private racks produced sustained decoder stalls and downstream 502/504s. The incident window was 22:08–23:05 UTC on 2026-11-09; residual jitter persisted intermittently until the hotpatch.
- What we did: Evelyn executed the rolling KV cache rebuild and pinned kernel selection on vc-11/12/13. Marissa coordinated customer throttling and the 10% hosted canary. We reverted the context cap after verifying stability.
- Outcome: P95 returned to ~340ms within 18 minutes of the final rollback and decoder 5xx dropped to baseline (<0.2%). Throughput returned to ~98% of prior baseline.
- Next action items (owner):
   * SRE: add a guard to detect cache-eviction storms and auto-balance hotspots (Evelyn).
   * Product: add a private-runtime kernel selection guard in the scheduler (Laura).
   * CS/Customer: runway plan for a second canary and capacity insurance (Marissa + StratusCare).

We will share a formal incident report (timeline, graphs, config diffs, and a finalized runbook) by EOD tomorrow. For the exec sync, we recommend a 30-minute run-through covering incident cause, fix, and the product-level guardrails we’ll commit to in Q1.

If StratusCare wants a credit for the impact window we’ll route the request through procurement (copied). Connor, please keep the deal owner looped until the runbook is finalized.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
